english.title: Fail to comply with requirement of relevant officer performing maritime enforcement functions – immigration
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement, namely **(..STATE REQUIREMENT..), made by **(..NAME OF OFFICER..), a relevant officer performing functions under Part A1 of Schedule 4A to the Immigration Act 1971
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph K1(1)(b) and (4) of Schedule 4A to the Immigration Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), the defendant without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement, namely **(..STATE REQUIREMENT..), made by **(..NAME OF OFFICER..), a relevant officer performing functions under Part A1 of Schedule 4A to the Immigration Act 1971.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limits for prosecutions:
6 months

Note
In relation to an offence committed before the coming into force of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.
